heroHeadline: HELSINGBORG T-3: SWEDEN LOCKS DOWN AIRSPACE — KRISTERSSON/MALMER STENERGARD T-3 BRIEF; UKRAINE FM SYBIHA CONFIRMED; RUTTE UKRAINE PLEDGE FAULT LINE HOLDS; PRE-MINISTERIAL MAY 20; FMM MAY 21–22
heroSubtitle: On May 18, 2026 — T-3 before the Helsingborg emergency NATO Foreign Ministers Meeting (May 21–22) — Sweden activated the summit's operational security perimeter as PM Kristersson and FM Malmer Stenergard held a joint pre-ministerial press briefing at Rosenbad, Stockholm. Swedish Police issued a temporary airspace restriction over Helsingborg effective 10:00 CEST today through May 22, 22:00 — covering the Clarion Hotel Sea U ministerial venue, the Sofiero Castle informal dinner, and approach corridors over the Øresund Strait. NATO separately confirmed Ukrainian FM Andrii Sybiha will participate at Helsingborg, giving Kyiv direct representation at the table where the Rutte 0.25% GDP Ukraine pledge fate will be decided. The central fault line: France and the UK continue to withhold support for the 0.25% GDP Ukraine military pledge (~$143B/year), while Baltic states, Poland, the Netherlands, and the Nordic allies push for adoption — the consensus requirement across all 32 allies makes adoption in its current mandatory form uncertain. Rutte's pre-ministerial press conference remains on for May 20 at NATO HQ Brussels. Background arc: May 17 — T-4 pre-ministerial consultations; May 15 — Army grilled in Congress on Poland ABCT cancellation (Pentagon gave 'just a couple of days' notice); May 14–15 — Rubio 'what's the purpose of the alliance?' after Spain denied Iran war bases; May 14 — CNN confirms 10,200+ troop scope (Germany 5,000 + Poland ABCT 4,700 + missile battalion 500); May 13 — B9+Nordic 'NATO 3.0' + Rutte 0.25% pledge; May 12 — EU FAC Defence; May 9 — Rasmussen 'disintegrating'; May 7 — 'terror incubators'; May 1 — Germany 5,000 withdrawal. Next: Rutte pre-ministerial brief May 20; Helsingborg FMM May 21–22; Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8, 2026.
